chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "If the deceased leaves only his paternal grandfather (father of his father) and his maternal grandmother (mother of his mother), then the grandmother receives one-third and the grandfather receives the remainder."

He said: "And if he leaves his paternal grandfather, his paternal grandfather's father, his maternal grandmother, and his maternal grandmother's mother, then the maternal grandmother receives one-third; the maternal grandmother's mother is excluded (saqat), and the remainder goes to the paternal grandfather; the paternal grandfather's father is excluded."

key_terms.قِبَلِ: From the side of / Lineage of

ai.seo_question: How is the estate divided among grandparents when they are the only heirs?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific distribution of the estate among grandparents when they are the sole heirs, establishing the principle of 'thuluth' (one-third) for the grandmother and the remainder for the grandfather. It further details the exclusion (saqat) of more distant grandparents in favor of the closer paternal and maternal lines, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precise lineage tracing in inheritance law. This ruling is foundational in the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for resolving conflicts between competing sets of grandparents.
